questions.q: A body travels $102.5 \mathrm{~m}$ in $\mathrmn^{\text {th }}$ second and $115.0 \mathrm{~m}$ in $(\mathrm{n}+2)^{\text {th }}$ second. The acceleration is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Given, } 102.5=\mathrm{u}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}(2 \mathrm{n}-1) \& \\
& 115=\mathrm{u}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}(2 \mathrm{n}+3) \\
& \Rightarrow 102.5=\mathrm{u}+\mathrm{an}-\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \& \\
& 115=\mathrm{u}+\mathrm{an}+\frac{3 \mathrm{a}}{2} \\
& 12.5=2 \mathrm{a} \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=6.25 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle starts with an initial velocity of $10 . 0\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$~along $x$-direction and accelerates uniformly at the rate of $2 . 0ms^{- 2}$. The time taken by the particle to reach the velocity of $60 . 0ms^{- 1}$& is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

$v = 60ms^{- 1}u = 10ms^{- 1}a = 2ms^{- 2}$

Using the equation~$v = u + at$, we get

$60 = 10 + 2t ⇒ t = \left(60 - 10\right)2 ⇒ t = 25s$

questions.q: An object of mass $5$ kg is thrown vertically upwards from the ground. The air resistance produces a constant retarding force of $10N$ throughout the motion. The ratio of time of ascent to the time of descent will be equal to : [Use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$].
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force while going upward will be& $mg + R = 50 + 10 = 60N$

$⇒ {a}_{up} = \dfrac{60}{5} = 12ms^{- 2}$

Similarly,~Net force while going downward~will be~$mg - R = 40N$

$⇒ {a}_{d} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8ms^{- 2}$

Since~

$h = \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{a}_{up}{tup}^{2}}{{a}_{d}{td}^{2}} = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{tup}{td} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{12}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

questions.q: The velocity-time graph of an object moving along a straight line is shown in figure. What is the distance covered by the object between $t=0$ to $t=4 \mathrm{~s}$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Distance travelled = displacement when direction of velocity remains constant
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \text { Distance } & =\text { Area } \\ & =\frac{1}{2}(2 \mathrm{~s}+4 \mathrm{~s})(10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}) \\ & =30 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The position co-ordinates of a particle moving in a $3D$ coordinate system is given by

$x = acos ⁡ \omegat$

$y = asin ⁡ \omegat$

and $z = a\omegat$

The speed of the particle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$x = acos ⁡ \omegat$

$y = asin ⁡ \omegat$

$z = a\omegat$

${v}_{x} = - a\omegasin ⁡ \omegat$

${v}_{y} = a\omegacos ⁡ \omegat$

${v}_{2} = a\omega$

$= \sqrt{{\left(- a\omegasin ⁡ \omegat\right)}^{2} + {\left(a\omegacos ⁡ \omegat\right)}^{2} + {\left(a\omega\right)}^{2}}$

$= a\omega\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: The velocity of a particle is $v = \left({v}_{0} + gt + Ft^{2}\right)ms^{- 1}$.~Its position is $x = 0$~at $t = 0;$ then its displacement after time $( t = 1s )$ is :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Area under velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled by the body in a given time.
Statement II: Area under acceleration-time graph is equal to the change in velocity in the given time.
In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The definition of displacement is given by the product of velocity and time.

$∫ vdt = ∆ x =$displacement of body in given time.

Distance is a scalar~quantity and displacement is a vector quantity defined by the shortest distance between the initial and the final position.

Acceleration is defined by the rate of change of velocity.
$∫ adt = ∆ v =$change in velocity in given time.

Thus, the area under the velocity time graph gives the displacement of the body and the area under the acceleration time graph gives the change in velocity of the body.

questions.q: A person is standing in an elevator. In which situation, he experiences weight loss ?
options: When the elevator moves upward with constant acceleration
When the elevator moves downward with constant acceleration
When the elevator moves upward with uniform velocity
When the elevator moves downward with uniform velocity
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the pseudo force acting on the person is in opposite direction to the weight then the person will experience weight loss. The direction of the pseudo force is opposite to the direction of the frame of reference.

Hence, B& is the correct answer.

questions.q: A bullet is fired into a fixed target looses one third of its velocity after travelling $4$ cm. It penetrates further $D \times {10}^{- 3}m$ before coming to rest. The value of $D$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the bullet just enters the target, its equation of motion is given by

$v^{2} - u^{2} = 2aS . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

\left(\dfrac{2u}{3}\right)$2 = u^{2} + $2 \left(-$a\right) \left(4 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)⇒ $\dfrac{4u^{2}}{9} =$u^{2} - 2a \left($4 $\times {10}^{- 2}\right)$⇒ \dfrac{5u^{2}}{9} =$2a \left(4 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) \ldots \left(2\right)$

When the bullet stops inside the target, its equation of motion can be written as

$0 = \left(\dfrac{2u}{3}\right)2 + 2 \left(-a\right)\left(x\right) . . . \left($3\right)$

Equation (3) implies that

\dfrac{4u^{2}}{9} =$2ax . . . \left(4\right)$

Dividing equation (2) by equation (4), we have

$\dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 2}}{x}⇒ x = \dfrac{16}{5} \times {10}^{- 2}⇒ x = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}m = 32 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

Hence, $D = 32$.

$

questions.q:
Two trains $A$ and $B$ of length $l$ and $4l$ are travelling into a tunnel of length $L$ in parallel tracks from opposite directions with velocities $108kmh^{- 1}$ and $72kmh^{- 1},$ respectively. If train $A$ take $35s$ less time than train $B$ to cross the tunnel then, length $L$ of tunnel is:

(Given $L = 60l$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time taken for& $A$

$\Delta{t}_{A} = \dfrac{l + L}{VA}$

The time taken for~$B$

$\Delta{t}_{B} = \dfrac{4l + L}{VB}$

It is given that~$B$~takes more time than~$A$. So,

$⇒ \dfrac{4l + L}{20} - \dfrac{l + L}{30} = 35$

$⇒ \dfrac{64l}{20} - \dfrac{61l}{30} = 35$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{35 \times 600}{700} = 30m$

Therefore,

$L = 1800m$.

$v^{2} = \left(v '\right)2 + 2ad$

solving, we get

$v ' = \sqrt{\dfrac{v^{2} + u^{2}}{2}}$

questions.q:
A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of $360 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ at an altitude of 2 km , drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point O , 20 s after it is dropped. Displacement of ' O ' from the position of helicopter where the object was released is :
(use acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and neglect air resistance)

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{u}=360 \times \frac{5}{18}=100 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{u} \times \mathrm{t}=2 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{H}=\frac{\mathrm{t}^2 \mathrm{~g}}{2} \\ & \mathrm{H}=\frac{400 \times 10}{2} \\ & \mathrm{H}=2000 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \mathrm{D}=\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{H}^2} \\ & \mathrm{D}=2 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~km}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle is moving unidirectional on a horizontal plane under the action of a constant power supplying energy source. The displacement (s) − time (t) graph that describes the motion of the particle is (graphs are drawn schematically and are not to scale):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here Power is constant,
Hence,& $P = Fv = mav = av = constant .$

$av = kv\dfrac{dv}{dx} \times v = k{∫}_{0}^{v}v^{2}dv = k{∫}_{0}^{x}dx ∴ v = \left(3k\right)1 / 3 \times \left($x\right)1 / 3 ⇒ v = A \left($x\right)1 / 3whereA = \left($3k\right)1 / 3 = constant . . . . \left($1\right)$

Also,~$v = $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$∴ $\dfrac{dx}{dt} ==A\left(x\right)1 / 3 ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{d}\dfrac{dx}{\left(x\right)1 / 3} =A{∫}_{0}^{t}dt$

Simplifying further we get,

$⇒ d = A \left(t\right)3 / 2 . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations~ \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$~its clear that the graph won't be straight line so first & third options cant be correct.
Now, from equation~ \left($1\right)$~its clear that when~$x$~is increased then the slope~\dfrac{ds}{dt}~should also increase which is possible in second option. Hence option~$2$ \text{ and } is correct. \text{ and }

$

questions.q: A car travels a distance of $x$~with speed ${v}_{1}$ and then same distance $x$~with speed ${v}_{2}$ in the same direction. The average speed of the car is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average velocity of car is:

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{Total displacement}{Total time}$

As the car is travelling along a straight line without turning, the magnitude of total displacement is same as the distance covered.~

The time taken to cover the first half is~$\dfrac{x}{v1}$~and the time taken to cover the second half is~$\dfrac{x}{v2}$

$∴ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{x}{v1} + \dfrac{x}{v2}}$

$⇒ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{2x\left({v}_{1}{v}_{2}\right)}{{v}_{1}x + {v}_{2}x} = \dfrac{2{v}_{1}{v}_{2}}{{v}_{1} + {v}_{2}}$

questions.q: A car covers $AB$ distance with first one-third at velocity ${v}_{1}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, second one-third at ${v}_{2}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ and last one-third at ${v}_{3}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. If ${v}_{3} = 3{v}_{1}, {v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{1} = 11\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, then the average velocity of the car is _____ $\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the total distance be& $d$.

Time taken to cover~\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)rd$~of total distance is~${t}_{1} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{1}}$.

Time taken to cover~\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)rd$~of total distance is~${t}_{2} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{2}}$.

Time taken to cover~\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)rd$~of total distance is~${t}_{3} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{3}}$.

Average speed$= \dfrac{Totaldistance}{Totaltime}$

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{d}{\dfrac{d}{3{v}_{1}} + \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{2}} + \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{3}}}$

$⇒ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{3\left({v}_{1}{v}_{2}{v}_{3}\right)}{{v}_{1}{v}_{2} + {v}_{2}{v}_{3} + {v}_{3}{v}_{1}}$

Here,~${v}_{1} = 11ms^{- 1}$, then,~${v}_{3} = 33ms^{- 1}, {v}_{2} = 22ms^{- 1}$

${V}_{avg} = \dfrac{3 \times 11 \times 22 \times 33}{\left(11 \times 22\right) + \left(22 \times 33\right) + \left(33 \times 11\right)} = 18ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: If the velocity of a body related to displacement $x$~is given by $v = \sqrt{5000 + 24x}ms^{- 1},$~then the acceleration of the body is _________~$ms^{- 2} .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that the rate of change of linear velocity is called linear acceleration,& $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{dv \times dx}{dt \times dx} = \dfrac{vdv}{dx}$

$⇒ a = \sqrt{5000 + 24x} \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5000 + 24x}} \times 24= 12ms^{- 2}$.

questions.q: A tennis ball is dropped on to the floor from a height of $9 . 8m$. It rebounds to a height $5 . 0m$. Ball comes in contact with the floor for $0 . 2s$. The average acceleration during contact is ______~$ms^{- 2}$. [Given~$g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The speed of ball just before collision with ground is& ${v}_i^{2} = 0 + 2g{h}_{i}$

~$⇒ {v}_{i} = \sqrt{2g{h}_{i}}$

$= \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 9 . 8}$

$= 14ms^{- 1} \left(Downward\right)$

The speed of ball just after collision is~$0 = {v}_f^{2} - 2g{h}_{f}$

$⇒ {v}_{f} = $\sqrt{2g{h}_{f}}

$= $\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 5}

$= 10ms^{- 1} \left(Upward\right)$

Average acceleration of ball is~\left|\overset{→}{a}avg\right| = \left|\dfrac{\Delta\overset{→}{v}}{\Deltat}\right| = \dfrac{{v}_{f} - \left(- {v}_{i}\right)}{t} = \dfrac{10 + 14}{0 . 2} = \dfrac{24}{0 . 2} =120ms^{- 2}$.

$

questions.q: The speed versus time graph for a particle is shown in the figure. The distance travelled (in $m$) by the particle during the time interval~$t = 0$~to~$t = 5$~$s$& will be __________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given graph is a speed-time graph.

The distance travelled by a particle is equal to the area under the speed-time graph.

From the graph, the shape of the area under the curve from $t = 0$ to $t = 5$ s is a triangle.

First, find the speed at $t = 5$ s. The graph is a straight line passing through the origin. From the points on the graph, at $t = 4$ s, the speed is $u = 8$ m/s.

The slope of the line (acceleration) is $\dfrac{8 - 0}{4 - 0} = 2$ m/s^2$.

Therefore, the speed at $t = 5$ s is $u = 2 \times 5 = 10$ m/s.

The distance is the area of the triangle with base $b = 5$ s and height $h = 10$ m/s.

$\text{Distance} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$

$\text{Distance} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10$

$\text{Distance} = 25 m

questions.q: A body moves on a frictionless plane starting from rest. If $S_n$ is distance moved between $t=n-1$ and $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}-1}$ is distance moved between $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}-2$ and $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}-1$, then the ratio $\frac{\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}-1}}{\mathrm{~S}_{\mathrm{n}}}$ is  \left(1-\frac{2}{x}\right)$ for $\mathrm{n}=10$. The value of $x$ is ______.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & S_n=\frac{1}{2} a(2 n-1)=\frac{19 a}{2} \\ & S_{n-1}=\frac{1}{2} a(2 n-3)=\frac{17 a}{2} \\ & \frac{S_{n-1}}{S_n}=\frac{17}{19}=1-\frac{2}{x} \Rightarrow x=19\end{aligned}$
